name: Relative Abundance Calculator
seoDesc: Relative abundance turns raw counts into the share of the community each species represents — the input every diversity index, ordination and community table
summary:
Relative abundance turns raw counts into the share of the community each species represents — the input every diversity index, ordination and community table starts from. It returns community size, species 1 relative abundance, species 2 relative abundance and top three species combined, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator gives percentages, proportions and the cumulative total. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Relative Abundance
sections.html:
pᵢ = nᵢ ÷ N × 100

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
nᵢindividuals of species iindividuals
Ntotal individualsindividuals
pᵢrelative abundance%

sections.title: How do I use the Relative Abundance?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: species 1 of 40 individuals, species 2 of 25 individuals, species 3 of 15 individuals, species 4 of 10 individuals, species 5 of 6 individuals.

Substituting them into the formula gives community size of 96 individuals, species 1 relative abundance of 41.67%, species 2 relative abundance of 26.04%, top three species combined of 83.33%.

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• Relative abundance makes samples of different size comparable, which absolute counts do not.

  • Percentages hide effort: 100% of a sample of three individuals is not the same statement as 100% of a sample of 3 000.

  • In sequencing data relative abundance is read out of the number of reads per taxon and is usually reported after rarefying to a common depth.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Using relative abundance as if it were an absolute density.
  • Summing percentages from different samples.
  • Comparing relative abundances between studies that rarefied to different depths.

faq.q: How do I calculate relative abundance as a proportion?
faq.a: Divide the count by the total without multiplying by 100 — 0.4 rather than 40%.
They do, up to rounding; the calculator works from full precision so the small residual is only display.

faq.q: What does the Relative Abundance actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns community size, species 1 relative abundance, species 2 relative abundance and top three species combined. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
